13.text: chiefly to keep off the wind and snow from the entrance. It often has no

14.text: door; and in order to get in, one has to crawl in under the tent-cover. The

15.text: main tent is constructed in the ordinary way, only, for the most part, an old

16.text: cover is used, because it is likely to be damaged by the hearth-fire within.

17.text: This fire is kept up all day long; and on this account, as well as on account

18.text: of the well-sheltered entrance, the temperature of the tent is not very low,

19.text: usually 10°-12° above zero Fahrenheit, while outside it may range from 50°

20.text: to 60° below. The sledges are piled up near the tent, high enough not to be

21.text: covered by the drifting snow, and after this are tied with thongs to prevent

24.text: The sleeping-room is much larger than that of the movable tent, and

25.text: bears marked similarity to that of the Maritime Chukchee, only it is dirtier

26.text: and is made more carelessly. The usual dimensions are 5 feet in height, 8

27.text: feet in breadth, and 14-16 feet in length. It occupies the whole rear of

28.text: the tent, leaving only a small space on the sides for storing provisions. The

29.text: skin cover is made of fawn-skins taken late in the fall, the hair side out. It

30.text: is drawn tightly across a rectangular frame made of flat, narrow sticks. On

31.text: the outside it is covered with a thick layer of dried grass tied up in sheaves

32.text: and fastened side by side. The frame is so strong that a man can walk on

33.text: top of it. The whole structure is covered with a piece of tent-covering, with

34.text: the ends carefully tucked in below. The floor is covered with skins of the

35.text: thong-seal or of the walrus, and over them some scraps of reindeer-skin are

36.text: put for seats, while the bedding is rolled up and taken away during the day.

37.text: One or two lamps burn constantly within, to keep the place dry. There

38.text: is no kind of ventilation whatsoever: therefore the sleeping-room, although

39.text: warm enough, in course of time becomes very unclean, and acquires an odor

40.text: offensive even to the inmates. Notwithstanding the burning lamp, the skin

41.text: cover becomes damp and covered with mildew. When newly constructed,

42.text: the sleeping-room is dried by carrying in a pile of burning coals on an iron

43.text: pan. The same method is sometimes applied afterwards, though it is dangerous,
